title.narrative: Humanitarian Mine Action response in North East Syria

description.narrative: Contract related to: Humanitarian Mine Action response in North East Syria - As the conflict in Syria has entered its eleventh year, the living conditions of ordinary Syrians have worsened dramatically as a result of continued hostilities, deteriorating socio-economic conditions, and the external repercussions of the Russian war of aggression against Ukraine. In the North-East, human security in communities and existing camps is further deteriorating, with the recent and recurrent attacks on security forces and civilians recalling the risk of resurgence of Da¿esh. In this context, additional stabilisation efforts are needed to minimise the risk of any further radicalisation and recruitment by extremist groups, which remains a major threat, especially for vulnerable children and youth. This measure will promote safer access to protection and learning spaces for children and boys at risk of further radicalisation and recruitment. It will also strengthen the social and economic resilience of host communities, internally displaced persons, and returnees in an effort to address urgent and longer-term needs. Finally, it will ensure that land mines and explosive remnants of war are removed from community infrastructure to ensure safer access to community services for the target populations in urban and rural areas.

comment.narrative: of distinct series of biannual Mine Action reports developed and distributed. This series of reports outlines the level of EO contamination in NES and its impact Mine Action activities progress key challenges and evidencebased recommendations.

The report was shared through 2 different dissemination channels. As such it was first presented during the VII Brussels Conference and shared with all participants. It was further shared by emails to 101ckey stakeholders amongst donors NGO forum partners Whole of Syria coordination partners and ad hoc Mine Action specialists.The report was shared via a link to the reliefweb website to ensure that individuals not part of the mailing list can also find it online.

title.narrative: Number of victims/incidents of mine/ERW explosions nationally

description.narrative: Number of victims/incidents of mine/ERW explosions nationally

comment.narrative: as of March 23 2057 victims were reported through the conduct of victim and accident reports by Mine Action organizations. As of this date iMMAP France estimated through open sources that 3036 persons were supposedly victims of EO explosions since 2016 in NES gap of 979 victims not verified through reports. The NESwide NTS will support in collecting additional verified information and improve knowledge decreasing knowledge gaps between opensource database and verified database from Mine Action organizations.
One victims gender could not be determined when reporting the accident.

title.narrative: Percentage of participants who report having benefitted from an event

description.narrative: Percentage of participants who report having benefitted from an event

comment.narrative: Humanitarian Mine Action Organizations participants international and national report having benefited from the MASGW coordination meetings and adhoc meetings hosted by iMMAP.

3 MASGW partners focal points failed to respond to the survey despite numerous reminders many focal points on leaves during this period. Thus this result reflects the views of only half partners. For the endline survey iMMAP France will combine the methodology with individual meetings to ensure all partners feedback are collected. The survey will also be maintained as it is anonymous and encourage more transparent and uninfluenced answers. Out of 3 responders 2 assessed that the MASGW coordination is facilitating their programs implementation and that this mechanism is recommended. 1 partner answered that such platform was partially helpful only. After discussion this partner is mostly frustrated by the lack of additional endorsement iMMAP France should receive to act as an authority instead of the NESMAO as UNMAS can be mandated in certain context. All feedback collected through this survey will be analyzed by the team presented to the MASGW partners and follow up actions drafted in a 6month plan. Calculation methodology Really helpful 5 Helpful 4 Partially helpful 2.5 not helpful 0. Final score 10.5 15

comment.narrative: iMMAP leads formal Mine Action Sub Working Group MASWG monthly coordination meetings with HMA implementing partners.

The MASWG gathers all international Mine Action organizations on a monthly basis. No MASWG meeting could be held in October 2022 as the projects launch was delayed by one month due to a delayed receipt of the grant agreement. Similarly no MASWG was held in September 2023 as partners cancelled it several times due to their internal agendas challenges were raised during this month to engaged actors. In parallel iMMAP France through this action launched an additional operational meeting to empower the NES Mine Action authorities and improve its coordination with international and national Mine Action organizations. One meeting was conducted in July 2023 and added to this result.
